description:
About the Position

Utrecht University's Faculty of Veterinary Medicine is recruiting two locum positions in equine reproduction for a five-month period. The locums provide temporary clinical capacity in the equine reproduction unit, covering routine and emergency reproductive work during a staffing transition, alongside the unit's permanent team.

The roles involve reproductive examinations, treatments and assisted-reproduction procedures in client horses, participation in the clinical rota and case handover documentation. Given the faculty's teaching mission, the locums also support students on clinical placements under supervision, keeping continuity in both service and education.

Candidate Profile

Applicants are qualified equine veterinarians with experience in reproduction work and eligibility to practise in the Netherlands. Both positions are five-month temporary contracts on the university's veterinary staff scale, with the standard application deadline published in the vacancy. Proficiency in Dutch for client contact is required; the clinical team works in English where needed.

Highlights

  • Temporary clinical cover in equine reproduction
  • Reproductive examinations and treatments
  • Participation in the clinical service rota
  • Student supervision support
  • Five-month salaried contracts, veterinary staff scale
  • Fixed closing date via the Utrecht recruitment portal

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
